dialogue:
Person1: Why the empty cage?
Person2: That one was for you. But I thought I'd wait and see how you behave when Supergirl gets here. I'd hate to lose you, Ethan.

Person1: I've heard the kidnapping story, so save it.  I know you're mixed up in all this, Dude, and I don't care what you're trying to take off her husband.  That's your business.  All I'm saying is, I want mine.
Person2: Yeah, well, right man, there are many facets to this, uh, you know, many interested parties.  If I can find your money, man-- what's in it for the Dude?
Person1: Of course, there's that to discuss. Refill?
Person2: Does the Pope shit in the woods?
Person1: Let's say a 10% finder's fee?
Person2: Okay, Jackie, done.  I like the way you do business.  Your money is being held by a kid named Larry Sellers. He lives in North Hollywood, on Radford, near the In-and-Out Burger. A real brat, but I'm sure your goons'll be able to get it off him, mean he's only fifteen and he's flunking social studies.  So if you'll just write me a check for my ten per cent. . . of half a million. . . fifty grand.

Person1: I'm thinking of moving on, Alex. This relationship doesn't feel right anymore.
Person2: After everything we've been through? You won't find anyone else who treats you like I do.
Person1: Maybe that's the problem. I need space and independence. It feels like you're trying to control everything.
Person2: I just want the best for you, for us.
Person1: I need to figure out what's best for me on my own.

Person1: As they age they contribute to a sum that is the kindling from which all future life comes.  To feel it, to know it, is to be in touch with the will of every living thing.
Person2: I do not think I like the sound of that.
Person1: It does not feel nearly as frightening as it sounds.  But the consequences of such feelings can be very frightening. For it gives you great strength.  The strength of _knowledge_.  The ability to stand between the giving of what has always been to what will always be.
Person2: I feel hardly nothing.
Person1: You have not been fully trained. But you will learn.  And you will be good, I can feel that.  You have apt- itude.  This is why our friend is so concerned.
Person2: But why be so concerned about me?
Person1: This power is divided amongst you, me, and others like cuts in a pie. But the cuts are not equal.  Some, like you and he, have more.  Much more.
Person2: And you?
Person1: I am a small player.  But if by helping you I can keep that monster from being the last, then perhaps my life has meant something.
Person2: I am not ready for this.
Person1: You must be.  You have responsibilities. You must learn the rules.  You can never attract attention to yourself, never show the side that will draw others to you.  You will always know when you are in the presence of another.  Beware. But more importantly Conor MacLeod, will be your battle against time.  In the coming years you will see kingdoms rise then rot like wheat.  People will become a transitory, pathetic lot.  The only constant you will know will be the others and the tradition their greed and quest represent.  But life without morality, without the ability to truly taste the sweetness of wine and love, is no life at all.  That is how the others exist.  Nothing more than walking corpses living only to slaughter each other in an insane quest to be the last.  Keep your soul sewed to the earth.  Do not become one of them.
Person2: Of course.
Person1: You are young, inexperienced.  You do not know what time can do.  How it can sap all pity, all love.
Person2: That is not me.
Person1: With the proper tools, Conor, a naive man can be much more dangerous than an evil one.

Person1: Power cells.
Person2: They're coming.
Person1: Strange, not doin' a run-up on the main drive yet.  Strange unless he told you the particulars of my escape.
Person2: I got the quick-and-ugly version.
Person1: An' now you're worried about a repeat of history?
Person2: Entered our minds.
Person1: I asked what you thought.
Person2: You scare me, Riddick. That's what you wanna hear, isn't it? There, I admit it, Can I get back to work now?

Person1: Oh, okay. I think I get it.
Person2: What do you get?
Person1: Well, they must be something sexual, because Ann gets freaked out by that shit. Are these tapes of you having sex with these girls or something?
Person2: Not exactly.
Person1: Well, either you are or you aren't. Which is it?
Person2: Why don't you let me tape you?
Person1: Doing what?
Person2: Talking.
Person1: About what?
Person2: Sex. Your sexual history, your sexual preferences.
Person1: What makes you think I'd discuss that with you?
Person2: Nothing.
Person1: You just want to ask me questions?
Person2: I just want to ask you questions.
Person1: And that's all?
Person2: That's all.
Person1: Is this how you get off or something? Taping women talking about their sexual experiences?
Person2: Yes.
Person1: Would anybody else see the tape?
Person2: Absolutely not. They are for my private use only.
Person1: How do we start?
Person2: I turn on the camera. You start talking.
Person1: And you ask questions, right?
Person2: Yes.
Person1: How long will it take?
Person2: That depends on you. One woman only used three minutes. Another filled up three two hour tapes.
Person1: Can I see some of the other tapes to get an idea of what --
Person2: No.
Person1: Do I sit or stand?
Person2: Whichever you prefer.
Person1: I'd rather sit. Are you ready?
Person2: Just a moment.

Person1: For a blur?
Person2: There is something there--don't ask, just trust me.

Person1: From time to time, even I have uttered the magic words.
Person2: Are you serious?
Person1: Yeah. No more. I'm finished with that shite.
Person2: Well, it's up to you.
Person1: I'm going to get it right this time. Going to get it set up and get off it for good.
Person2: Sure, sure. I've heard it before.
Person1: The Sick Boy method.
Person2: Yeah, well, it surely worked for him.
Person1: He's always been lacking in moral fibre.
Person2: He knows a lot about Sean Connery.
Person1: That's hardly a substitute.
Person2: you'll need one more hit.
Person1: No, I don't think so.
Person2: To see you through the night that lies ahead.

Person1: It was a long time ago... I met him at this place called Moke's... We... became friends... He told me about a job...
Person2: What job?
Person1: I don't remember... Anyway, Andy's okay...
Person2: He's got some messed up friends.

Person1: Six of us left. If we could get through that canyon and lose just one, that'd be quite a remarkable feat, huh? A good thing, right?
Person2: Not if I'm the one.
Person1: What if you're one of five?

Person1: By the way, Jeffrey, this story isn't going to the press and I'm going to ask you to consider all you've heard strictly confidential. Do not discuss this business with anyone, but me, or other police personnel. Got it?
Person2: Got it. Thanks for letting me in on as much as you did.
Person1: Come on. I'll drive you home. It's on my way.

Person1: See that wasn't so bad.
Person2: It was nothing.
Person1: Let's try it again, only this time I'm going to stick my tongue in your mouth. When I do that I want you to massage my tongue with yours. That's what first base is.
Person2: Okay.
Person1: Eyes closed.

Person1: There's a guard outside my door! I'm a prisoner, Nigel!  Do you understand that?
Person2: Dr. Argon would say we are all prisoners.
Person1: Argon is a lunatic!  I can't believe I was stupid enough to believe I could control him.  You heard what he said, Nigel.  He doesn't care if all of Calumet City is turned to Jell-O.  How can that not affect you?
Person2: Because I am a new man, Susan.  I am a man of vision.  Your problem, Susan, is that you're always looking down.  If you'd just look up you'd see the big picture and in the big picture men of vision do not dwell on what might be lost.  They focus on what can be gained.
Person1: Is that what Argon told you?
Person2: No!  Well, not those exact words.
Person1: Nigel, can't you see he's using you?
Person2: Of course he is, but at least there isn't a security guard outside my door.
Person1: You're afraid of him.
Person2: Who isn't?

Person1: How's school?
Person2: OK. OK. But now that I've got a job, I'11 probably stop going...
Person1: Don't do that...Sooner or later you'll be left empty-handed.
Person2: Why? What do you mean?
Person1: Toto, this isn't for you. For the moment, the Cinema Paradiso needs you, and you need the Cinema Paradiso. But it won't last...Some day you'll have other things to do, more important things...  That's right, more important. I know it. Now that I've lost my sight I see more. I see everything I didn't see before...  And it's all thanks to you, who saved my life. And I'll never forget it...  And don't put on that look. I haven't gone off my head yet. You want proof?

Person1: Says here you're getting Martin Weir for the part of Lovejoy.
Person2: Yeah, we're getting Martin.
Person1: No shit, come on. How you gonna do that?
Person2: I put a gun right here...  ...and I tell him, 'Sign the paper Marty or you are dead.' Like that.
Person1: I wonder, would that work?  You know who I see for Al Roxy? Harvey Keitel. The man could do it in his sleep.
Person2: Harvey Keitel. Yeah. Maybe. He was pretty good in the movie "Fingers".
Person1: I missed that one. Or, hey, you know who else? Morgan Freeman. You know Morgan?
Person2: Yeah, Morgan Freeman. But he's a colored guy.
Person1: So what? Where's it say in this script he's white? Color is what the part needs, man, somebody to do it has some style. The way it is now, Ronnie could do it, play himself, some cracked out asshole.  So whatta you think of the script?

Person1: Do you know what he's saying?
Person2: What who's saying?
Person1: Manzanita....  ... if one day I die, and you read this piece of paper, I want you to know how much I love you. Although I'll never see you again, Gypsy, Gypsy, your hair, your hair, your face, your face'

Person1: No, no, no.  Put it back on and take it off slowly.
Person2: Jesus, what kinda broad are you?
Person1: When you know how to make love, you'll know how to pitch.  Shh.  I love this part.

Person1: Ray, where do you keep the glasses?
Person2: Oh, is Shari here? Why didn't you just say so? Why are you giving me a song-and-dance about being tired?
Person2: Hi, Shari.
Person1: Who's Shari?
Person2: Who's --

Person1: Martha, you have to make a decision on her sanity as quickly as possible and not interfere with due process of law.
Person2: No... no, excuse me Eve. As quickly as I see fit.
Person1: The longer you take to make a decision, the more difficult it will be for us.
Person2: Why?
Person1: The bishop is breathing down our necks.
Person2: And the sooner she goes to prison, the better off she'll be?

Person1: It's a fake.
Person2: Give him the card.
Person1: But--
Person2: Can you follow simple directions?

Person1: Well, Elaine, this might be it if those guys on the ground don't think of something.
Person2: I just want you to know, I love you Ted and always will.
Person1: That might be the news we've been waiting for.

Person1: Got any booze in the house?
Person2: You don't drink "booze".
Person1: You do.
Person2: Eddie, if I wanted to make love with you again, I'd do it sober.

Person1: You know what my goal is? Before I die I want to make love to a woman from every country on earth.
Person2: You mean countries that are acknowledged by the UN...or like made up countires too?
Person1: What the hell does that mean?
Person2: Like Mamooli's country...

Person1: Vicki?... This is Batman. I thought I'd call and see how you're doing.
Person2: ... I know it's you, Bruce. I'm not going to talk to you unless we can discuss it...
Person1: Who's this 'Bruce'? Are you trying to make me jealous?
Person2: I'm serious, Bruce. We have to -- !

Person1: You put this inside your shirt -- when Tiger stabs your stomach -- it's full of pig's blood.  Gushes out everywhere!  It's really impressive.  Fantastic!  Better than the real thing!
Person2: So I pretend I'm dead.  You get gold, what do I get?
Person1: You get to come alive again in the country!
Person2: As, what, 'The Galloping Gladiator?!'
Person1: The point is you get to fight the easy country circuit, the small arenas, relax, live the good life!
Person2: Spend my days beheading country bumpkins?  I don't know, Proximo, who has better wine than you? Besides, I'm beginning to think of the Colosseum as my home.
Person1: But -- you have to go out there! I'll give you more than your one third!  When I get paid... just take the fall!  You're too hurt to fight and the man's a killer!
Person2: Pressures on, eh Proximo?  There's got to be a load of money in this. Why else would you toss a red hot commodity like me out the window?
Person1: It's absolutely not like that!  This is for your own good!  Come on get the rest of your armor on!

Person1: He's dead.
Person2: We bury the body. We disappear into the woods. Nobody knows.
Person1: No. This is the end of the road. There's a dead human being here. For all of his faults, he was a human being, and certainly a victim of his culture as much as anybody.
Person2: Forget him, Lila. We'll disappear. We'll never talk about it again. We'll never talk again period. I love you.
Person1: Puff, what happened to you is as much my fault as Nathan's. Maybe more so, because I knew it was wrong and I went along with it anyway. I'm taking responsibility for the murder. I want you to go back to your old life.
Person2: I won't let you do that. I shot the bastard. And I'm glad.
Person1: No. Go back to the woods. This is a sacrifice I need to make. In my world we have something called penance. It's another abstraction, but I had the concept drummed into my head during my years in the convent. It doesn't exist for you, and it shouldn't. See, I could never be free again anyway, so I might as well be in jail.
Person2: Then I'll live for both of us, Lila. I'll be the most free, truest animal in the whole forest. For both of us.
Person1: That's what I'm counting on.
Person2: But first I'll live among them, just long enough to testify before congress about the waywardness of humankind.
Person1: Okay. If you think it will help.

Person1: Hello.
Person2: Ambassador Han.
Person1: Yes.
Person2: Even if you deny the FBI is there, I will assume you are lying.

Person1: She said "If they get me".  They. Which means the whole sex-killer thing is a cover, which means somebody whacked her for a reason.
Person2: So the guy's not a sicko.
Person1: If he could do what's on that tape, he's a sicko.
Person2: Okay, so he's a freak who thinks he's sane pretending to be a freak. The point is, he was a hitter. Somebody wanted to shut her up.  But why not just put a little lead in her ear?
Person1: Because it had to look random.  Not connected to anything or anyone.  But then why give the rape to me?
Person2: That's where it gets a little strange.
Person1: And what about the guy that was following me?
Person2: Now you're really getting paranoid.

Person1: But you can't let her get involved now, Ben. Vader will destroy her.
Person2: She hasn't been trained in the ways of the Jedi the way you have, Luke... but the Force is strong with her, as it is with all of your family. There is no avoiding the battle. You must face and destroy Vader!

Person1: Hi.
Person2: I'd prefer it if you didn't speak to me.
Person1: I...
Person2: ...you know, there's nothing you could say, that could possibly make a difference, so, why don't you just save your breath.

Person1: What's the matter with you?
Person2: You are afraid!
Person1: Afraid ... of what?
Person2: -- of what happens after we die!
Person1: Are you plumb crazy, man! What do you think happens? We're buried -- that's all.
Person2: But what becomes of our souls?
Person1: Why do you fret about something that isn't there?
Person2: Don't say that -- I know it is --
Person1: All right -- so it's buried with you!
Person2: What if one hasn't a soul any more? What of that?
Person1: Huh? -- What's that?  Well -- what about it? Who cares, anyhow?
Person2: I do -- and I think you should too.
Person1: Stevens -- what's all this leading up to? You know something. Come on! Out with it -- you know something about me!

Person1: I'm sorry. After careful consideration, I regretfully have to decline.
Person2: C'mon, man, I'm just asking for one Superbowl ring.
Person1: In exchange for eternal damnation of your soul? You're too nice of a guy for me to want to do that to you, Mr. Marino.
Person2: You did it for Namath.
Person1: Yeah, but Joe was coming here anyways. Just go back to Earth and enjoy your records and the Hall of Fame and the beautiful family and all that.
Person2: This is bullshit, man.  I'm gonna win the Superbowl this year, with or without you!
Person1: Now you're talking.

Person1: I'm feeling too good to fight with you, but that isn't what I said - I said you snoop.  For instance, what were you doing around my hotel the other night?
Person2: Begging your pardon, I haven't been down the bowery in years!

Person1: And besides, when you say I make tax- deductible excuses you make me out a criminal.
Person2: You couldn't be a criminal if you committed a major crime.
Person1: I wish I were. Not an active criminal but... a nice guy with the conscience of a criminal.  Next best thing to no conscience at all.
Person2: I have to go, Sam.
Person1: I can come down next week.
Person2: No.
Person1: Not even just to see you, to have lunch... in public?
Person2: We can see each other, we can even have dinner... but respectably, in my house with my mother's picture on the mantel and my sister helping me broil a big steak for three!
Person1: And after the steak... do we send Sister to the movies and turn Mama's picture to the wall?
Person2: Sam! No!
Person1: All right.

Person1: Did they give you a rough time?
Person2: No.  You bastard. You knew they'd come back.
Person1: No, I didn't,  Does Albert Swift still live over the ferry?
Person2: Get knotted.
Person1: All right. All right. I want to square things with you first.
Person2: Oh yes? How?

Person1: Who was it?
Person2: What?
Person1: On the phone. Was it for you?
Person2: I don't know, he didn't say anything.
Person1: Uh-huh. So how do you know it was a he?
Person2: You got a girl--am I screwing something up by being here?

Person1: John?  John where are you going?
Person2: I think this heat is making me crazy.  I was crazy to come back here, I'm crazy for listening to anyone in this town, and I'd sure as hell be crazy if I spent another minute in this place.
Person1: John, please--
Person2: I don't know what I was thinking, but I can't do it.
Person1: What are you talking about?
Person2: Kill someone.  I can't do it.
Person1: Is it so bad?  It would be quick. He wouldn't even have to feel it.

Person1: ... No, I went in for more improving pastimes.  Philosophy classes, language courses, European history, all that lark. Did you know that in Paris in the Eighteenth Century there were more rats in people's houses than there were people in people's houses.
Person2: Sounds like Beverly Hills.
Person1: Here, are you always this sarky?
Person2: Sarcastic, moi?  Maybe I'll mellow when my ship comes in.  It's expected any day now.  I'm all packed and ready to go.
Person1: Weren't you on a television series?
Person2: If it played in England somebody owes me money.  Who told you that -- Eddie?
Person1: Said it went on for donkey's years.
Person2: Three seasons.  They found that's the limit of human tolerance when it comes to following the adventures of a family of Mormons on the Chisum Trail.  I was wife number three -- the ingenue.
Person1: Oh, it just ended, then.
Person2: Now who's being sarcastic?
Person1: When you've lost as many years as I have, love, puts things in perspective, know what I mean.
Person2: I'm sorry.  I guess the rest of us have no excuse for wondering where the time went.  It must've been the bars.

Person1: We gotta get you to a doctor.
Person2: It's okay.  Forget it.
Person1: Forget it?  Are you crazy? Let me see it.

Person1: 'The heir to the fortune must wear the Mayfair pendant an her wedding day.'  We should all have to suffer such burdens.
Person2: Then you wear it.
Person1: C'mon now - give a little nod to Mayfair tradition.

Person1: Mom?
Person2: I've been so worried, dear. where are you?
Person1: Nashville.
Person2: Oh... Well.
Person1: The car broke down.
Person2: Oh, well, I knew that before you- even left. I told you, 'Kenny, that old Nash won't make it down the road.'  But you had to go.
Person1: Well, I got to Nashville. That's pretty far.
Person2: Next you'll be sick.
Person1: I feel really good.
Person2: How are you going to pay when you get sick?
Person1: I'm in a rooming house with Mr. Green.
Person2: Green?  Not Owen Green. Owen Green embezzled money from your grandfather
Person1: I don't know his first name.
Person2: Bet the sheets are grey.
Person1: No. No, they're white. He's got a nice dog.
Person2: Worst time at year for dogs is when they get fungus.
Person1: Fungus?
Person2: He doesn1t have fungus, does he?
Person1: I don't think so.
Person2: Well, you'll get it, skin as sensitive as yours.
Person1: How do you know if they do?

Person1: Now what are you doing?
Person2: Describing you. A square from out there. I mean you're nowhere.  Miss Four Corners.
Person1: What made you want to be a fighter?
Person2: I had to scrap all my life. Figured I might as well get paid for it. When I was a kid my old man got killednever mind how. Charley and I was put in a placethey called it a Children's Home. Some home! I run away and peddled papers, fought in club smokers and  But what am I runnin' off at the mouth for? What do you care?
Person1: Shouldn't we care about everybody?
Person2: What a fruitcake you are!
Person1: Isn't everybody part of everybody else?
Person2: Gee, thoughts! Alla time thoughts!  You really believe that drool?
Person1: Terry!
Person2: Want to hear my philosophy? Do it to him before he does it to you.
Person1: Our Lord said just the opposite.
Person2: I'm not lookin' to get crucified. I'm lookin' to stay in one piece.
Person1: I never met such a person. Not a spark of romance or sentiment or or human kindness in your whole body.
Person2: What do they do for you, except get in your way?
Person1: And when things get in your way or people you just knock them aside get rid of Them is that your idea?
Person2: Listen get this straight don't look at me when you say them things. It wasn't my fault what happened to your brother. Fixing Joey wasn't my idea... .
Person1: Why, Terry, who said it was?
Person2: Well, nobody, I guess. But that Father Barry, I didn't like the way he kept lookin' at me.
Person1: He was looking at everybody the same way. Asking the same question.
Person2: Yeah, yeah... .  This Father Barry, what's his racket?
Person1: His racket?
Person2: You've been off in daisyland, honey. Everybody's got a racket.
Person1: But a priest...?

Person1: Hungry?
Person2: Just some coffee.
Person1: I'm not surprised. After all that humble pie...
Person2: Nothing of the kind. Karen and I had a nice talk.
Person1: Heart to heart? Woman to woman? Including a casual reference to the part of "Cora" - and your hopes of playing it.
Person2: I discussed it very openly. I told her that I had spoken to Lloyd - and that he was interested.
Person1: She mentioned, of course, that Margo expects to play the part?
Person2: Oddly enough - she didn't say a word about Margo. Just that she'll be happy to do what she can to see that I play the part.

Person1: If you got a problem with me, why are we dancing?
Person2: Yorgi asked me to.
Person1: You do everything Yorgi says?
Person2: Go to hell.
Person1: It's gonna be like that, huh? You got all bent out of shape as soon as he started dancing with someone else. Why's that?
Person2: Mind your business.
Person1: Did you guys used to date? That's it, right? He broke your heart and you're still soft on him. That's funny, it don't seem to fit with a tough broad like you.

Person1: You have to tell me what you're doing with my Venom.
Person2: You must show me your secrets, blossom, before I show you mine.

Person1: She doesn't belong here, Sean.  Let her go.
Person2: She wouldn't  be here if it wasn't for you, Hunt.  from this moment you're responsible for what happens to her, and if you're looking out for her well-being, I suggest you advise her to pick up the gun and bring it to me.  Ball's in your court, Hunt.  What've you got to say? Nyah's waiting for your answer.

Person1: He should have armed himself if he was gonna decorate his saloon with the body of my friend.
Person2: I guess you are Three-Fingered Jack out of Missouri, killer of women and children.
Person1: I have done that... killed women and children... I have killed most everything that walks or crawls an' now I have come to kill you, Little Bill, for what you done to Ned.  Now step aside. boys.

Person1: I'll go out with you, or I'll stay here, and do anything you'd like for me to do... if you'll just do one thing. If you'll tell me that you love me.
Person2: You can sing the song.
Person1: You know what, you are never satisfied.
Person2: That's right, hand.

Person1: Are you kidding?!  You wouldn't even be a crumb on her table!  You don't see that?!
Person2: Eve?!
Person1: Well, I'm trying to educate him!  It's nothing personal.
Person2: Adam,  I think for you, we should go for "sweet."

Person1: You cannot stay here...I'm sorry.
Person2: You and I are going to move my father right now...to another room on another floor...Can you disconnect those tubes so we can wheel the bed out?
Person1: Absolutely not!  We have to get permission from the Doctor.
Person2: You've read about my father in the papers.  You've seen that no one's here to guard him.  Now I've just gotten word that men are coming to this hospital to kill him.  Believe me and help me.
Person1: We don't have to disconnect them, we can wheel the stand with the bed.

Person1: No, no! I won't sign any pa- pers. You can't make me--
Person2: Hm--pressure-- To Buckley. That's all right. We'll talk later.

Person1: I didn't say that.  Why would I say that?
Person2: Well Daddy and I were thinking that sometimes people tell a story about what they wish would happen.
Person1: I don't want that to happen.  Why would I want that to happen?
Person2: Well you're telling your teachers and your friends --
Person1: Mass hysteria.
Person2: Maybe you're upset that Rachel moved in.
Person1: I'm not upset.  Why would I be upset?
Person2: Look if the truth is you don't feel like talking about this right now that's fine. But don't look me in the eye with a big smile on your face and lie to me. Cause there are only so many lies you're allowed to tell before it starts showing on your face.  You wind up looking like...

Person1: I'm not saying another word.  You damn fool.  He's a journalist.
Person2: Just tell me about Swann.  Or are you too scared?
Person1: He was a freak.  Everything he did was tainted.

Person1: Rose, this is Waski. His real name is Warren but we call him Waski. He doesn't like it much and I suppose someday we'll have to stop calling him that.
Person2: You can stop it right now.
Person1: When he was baby we called him "Wa Wa," a baby name, you know. You will find him a very good boy. His brother can be bad and so can his sister, but Waski is a very good boy. And as you can see he's beautiful.
Person2: Oh, Mother, cut it out.
